University of Copenhagen Confirms Data Breach Impacting Over 545,000 Individuals

Incident Overview

The University of Copenhagen has officially confirmed a significant cybersecurity breach that resulted in the unauthorized access of sensitive personal information belonging to more than 545,000 individuals. The university disclosed that attackers gained entry into a test environment, which served as a gateway to extract data including full names, national identity numbers (CPR), phone numbers, and email addresses.

Following an initial discovery of the incident, the university conducted a follow-up assessment, which revealed that an additional 20,000 staff and students had their campus access PIN codes exposed during the attack. The university’s IT department has since contained the breach, confirmed that no further systems were compromised, and successfully prevented additional unauthorized access.

University Response and Security Measures

In response to the exposure of physical access PINs, the university implemented immediate security protocols. This included restricting access to critical campus locations and redistributing new, secure access codes to affected staff and students. These campus areas have since been gradually reopened following the completion of these security measures.

As the breach falls under the jurisdiction of the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), the university has notified the Danish Data Protection Agency. An ongoing investigation is currently underway to determine the extent of the impact and necessary regulatory compliance steps.

Practical Implications and Risks

The exposure of such a large dataset of personal and contact information presents a significant risk to affected individuals. Security experts note that stolen data of this nature is frequently weaponized in targeted phishing campaigns. By utilizing legitimate personal details, attackers can create highly convincing, personalized emails that impersonate university departments or official services.

Common tactics observed in similar academic breaches include messages claiming that a user's email account is due for decommissioning or requiring immediate identity verification. These messages often direct victims to fraudulent login pages—typically disguised as Microsoft 365 portals—to harvest credentials for further unauthorized access or malware deployment.

How to Verify and Protect Your Data

  • Verification: The university has issued a formal notification on its official website. Students and staff should monitor their university-issued email accounts and the official portal for specific instructions regarding their data status.
  • Stay Vigilant: If you are a student, alumni, or staff member associated with the University of Copenhagen, exercise extreme caution with unsolicited emails, especially those requesting urgent action or credential verification.
  • Official Updates: For ongoing information regarding the investigation and official guidance, refer directly to the University of Copenhagen's public communications page at: https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/over-525-000-hit-in-massive-university-of-copenhagen-data-breach
